transcript: let's talk about some like it hot and I debated making this video but I wanna bring some nuance to this conversation so here is my defense for the character of Joe I know I know I know stick with me before I get into this massive spoilers for the musical some Like It Hot if you haven't seen it wanna go on blind go ahead and scroll now if you're sticking around just a reminder that the original Some Like a Hot film was about 2 cis men who witness a crime and have to disguise themselves as women in order to escape with their lives updated 2022 musical version Joe is still a cis man played by Christian Borla and Jerry played by non binary performer Jay Harrison Ghee is a character who in disguising themselves as Daphne comes to learn of their own gender fluidity there's been some very real criticisms about the character of Joe and I don't think they handled him perfectly I definitely would have made changes but one of the things that I'm seeing people who criticize the character of Joe say is that the existence of Daphne doesn't negate the existence of Joe well I definitely don't think that the existence of Daphne absolves the show of any criticism I do think that we lose some of the nuance when we ignore the fact that these 2 characters exist in the same musical because that's an important fact now there is a lot of very real transphobia in the world right now to the point where lawmakers are actively trying to take away rights from trans people and that hatred is dangerous and actively costs real lives and it is easy to hate something you don't understand which is why representation in media is so important both for trans people to be able to see other trans people existing but also for cis people to see trans people existing one of the great things about Some Like A Hot is we get to see the character of Daphne existing and being joyful and there is never once the fear of disclosure Daphne doesn't exist in a world with trans trauma in fact the only character who fears disclosure in Some Like a Hot is Joe Joe is a character who is forced into this disguise to save his own life and because the stakes are so high for him we get to see him experience gender dysphoria he actively throughout the show is talking about how he can't wait till they get to safety so he doesn't have to be Josephine anymore he talks about how hard it is for him to be a woman in the show where he feels like he's safe and then something else will happen that will force him back into that Josephine disguise again all this contrasted with daphne's very real gender euphoria they literally have a line in the first song where they put on the dress where they look in the mirror and go ah I think I love her and because both of these characters exist simultaneously we get to see essentially very real traumas that trans people go through told through a cis lens while the trans person gets to experience all of the joy and of course I would rather have original works of art being told by trans people geared towards trans people at the same time Broadway very much is a business and of course they have to sell tickets and it's proven that if you adapt an existing property it's a little easier to do that and ultimately I think there's something beneficial for cis people to see gender portrayed across these 2 characters even if yeah some of the jokes are very cringe
